messages:
emily: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak landed in canary we see a consistent ~8-12% host CPU overhead increase on short chat requests (<= 64 tokens). Traces point to parsing + streaming chunker hot paths.

emily: p99 latency +2x on tiny payloads, cost climb on tiny-batch workloads. Not seeing model-side time change.

raj: on it. Can you paste a perf top / flame for the worker PID? Also which canary cluster?

emily: canary: eu-west-ded-3, example perf snippet below (sampled over 30s during storm):

```
  12.4%  host_proc  [.] parse_stream::decode_frame
   9.7%  host_proc  [.] chunker::emit_fragment
   6.2%  host_proc  [.] http2::writev_small
   5.1%  host_proc  [.] tokenize::tokenize_inline
   4.8%  host_proc  [.] kv_cache::lookup_or_populate
   3.3%  libc.so   [.] write
```

emily: full flame attached to the triage ticket (link) — but the interesting part is parse_stream -> chunker -> writev_small chain.

mich: that writev_small jump smells like more small writes after the kernel change (maybe kernel selected a narrower batch path that flushes earlier). Any change to batching heuristics?

emily: yes, kernel-sel now prefers model kernels optimized for short sequences which also switched the runtime to use early-flush batching (smaller per-request batch hints). We thought it would reduce GPU tail but it appears host-side overheads dominate for small inputs.

raj: can we reproduce locally with the microbench harness? Steps I'd run:
- spin a worker with canary binary
- run grpcurl flood with 8-16 concurrent clients, payloads 8-64 tokens, collect perf and strace

mich: I already ran a quick strace. snippet:

```
write(5, "\x00\x01...", 512) = 512
writev(5, [{iov_base=0x..., iov_len=128}, {iov_base=0x..., iov_len=64}], 2) = 192
write(5, "\x00", 1) = 1  <-- lots of 1-byte writes
```

mich: the tokenization path seems to be emitting extra single-byte frames for the streaming protocol because chunker boundaries changed.

emily: P95 CPU per-request jumped from 17ms -> 29ms host-time on these tiny requests. Model kernel time dropped ~1ms, so net regression.

raj: two hypotheses: (A) earlier flushes cause more syscalls and smaller writev payloads; (B) KV cache unhappy — more lookups leading to extra copy/serialize during parse. Which perf counters show more syscalls?

emily: syscall count per request increased ~3x (from 10 -> ~32 syscalls) during the canary. KV cache hit-rate steady but lookup latency up ~30us (maybe due to extra copies).

mich: quick mitigation idea: re-enable pooled chunk-assembly (batch fragments in host memory before writev) for short requests only. That reduces number of writev calls. Also consider re-tuning batching hint so kernel-sel doesn't request early flush for <=64 tokens.

raj: agree. Also add a microbenchmark to ensure kernel selection policy includes a host-cost penalty for early-flush-heavy kernels. We already have metrics for GPU vs host; just add a small weight for syscalls-per-token.

emily: +1. I'll prototype pooled chunk-assembly toggle behind a runtime flag and canary it.

deploy-bot: deploy requested: emily/kernel-parse-pool-toggle -> canary eu-west-ded-3 (requested by emily).

sre-bot: alert: p99 latency increased (eu-west-ded-3) — 2026-03-21T12:14:02Z.

raj: action items: @emily implement toggle + perf harness tests; @mich run strace/flame for toggled vs untoggled; @raj add kernel-sel host-penalty heuristic and unit tests. If pooled assembly drops syscalls back to baseline and p99 regresses gone, we ship revert-free.

emily: timeline: will push toggle PR in next 2hrs. Low-risk change, runtime flag default off. Will attach benchmark artifacts.

mich: will run a 30min soak with 1k rps scaled to tiny payloads once PR is up.

raj: if that passes, schedule a canary ramp to 25% then 100%. Keep deploy-bot hooked for auto-rollback on p99 spike.

emily: also adding a small telemetry counter: host_small_writes_per_request to validate hypothesis in production without full flame runs.

mich: one more note — KV cache populate path does extra JSON serialization in the populate path. If we see populate op increase (it's cheap but at higher frequency it matters), we should inline a binary proto for cache-populate to avoid stringify cycles.

emily: noted — will measure populate op count in the harness.

raj: thanks all. Logging follow-ups in the perf triage ticket. If anyone sees otherwise, ping here. :thumbsup:

mich: quick test result (post-PR): pooled-assembly toggle ON -> syscall count drops from ~32 -> ~11, p95 host CPU goes 29ms -> 18ms, p99 back near baseline. Posting full numbers to ticket.

emily: great, I'll kick the canary ramp once deploy-bot confirms instrumented metrics.

deploy-bot: canary ramp started -> 25% eu-west-ded-3 at 2026-03-21T14:05:00Z. Monitoring p99 and host_small_writes_per_request.

sre-bot: p99 (canary, 25%) stable, no auto-rollback triggered.

emily: PR merged behind flag, plan to enable flag cluster-wide after 24h soak if metrics remain stable.

raj: follow-up: we should add a regression test that simulates 8-64 token requests and asserts syscalls-per-request stays below threshold when kernel-sel opts for short-sequence kernels. I'll pick this up tomorrow.

mich: good call. Also adding a perf gauge in CI to capture writev distribution (counts of write sizes) to catch regressions earlier.

emily: thanks y'all, closing the slack thread and moving next steps to the ticket.
